note.question: What determines most consumers in rural areas of many developing countries cannot afford to purchase certain livelihood improvement products such as home appliances?
note.overview: Most consumers in rural areas of many developing countries cannot afford to purchase certain livelihood improvement products such as home appliances. To improve consumer welfare and manufacturer profit, many governments launch different types of subsidy programs that offer subsidies to consumers, manufacturers, or both. Motivated by a subsidy program developed by the Chinese government in 2007, we present a parsimonious model to determine the optimal subsidy program in different settings so as to gain a better understanding about the conditions under which it is optimal for the government to subsidize consumers only, manufacturers only, or both.

models.name: Improving Consumer Welfare and Manufacturer Profit via Government Subsidy Programs model
models.summary: Most consumers in rural areas of many developing countries cannot afford to purchase certain livelihood improvement products such as home appliances. To improve consumer welfare and manufacturer profit, many governments launch different types of subsidy programs that offer subsidies to consumers, manufacturers, or both. Also, we find that governments can improve consumer welfare by developing subsidy programs that involve multiple (competing) manufacturers with different market sizes and adequate capacities.

conditions: The manufacturer subsidy takes the form of cost subsidy αc per unit, where c is the unit production cost and α ∈[0, 1) is the portion (a decision variable) of the cost to be borne by the government.
